findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the no-tests blocking policy with the doc's mapped-vs-no-tests convention: define how subprocess-attributed no-tests mutants are scored so strict/ratchet block real gaps without failing on behavior pinned only by subprocess interface tests.
evidence: Plan: strict requires 'every mutant is killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent; no-tests ... block'; ratchet: 'Added or edited functions must kill every mutant unless a survivor matches a reviewed equivalent fingerprint' and 'any new survivor/no-tests result' blocks.

docs/mutation-testing.md §'Score interpretation': 'coverage collected in the parent process cannot attribute those lines, so mutmut files them as no tests even though the behavior is pinned by the subprocess assertions'; the honest score uses mapped mutants 'with no-tests reported separately rather than folded into the denominator.'
Scores table: gates.py 376 no-tests, validate.py 223, next_batch.py 208, signing.py 110 — all from subprocess-attributed behavior, not gaps.
findings.finding: The gate treats mutmut `no-tests` as a blocking outcome (ratchet added/edited functions, every new result, and strict whole-shard), but the repo's mutation cores legitimately produce large no-tests populations from subprocess-driven interface tests that mutmut's in-process coverage map cannot attribute — so the rule would block on well-tested-but-unattributable mutants rather than real coverage gaps.
findings.location: Plan section (ratchet/strict mode definitions); AC 'Strict tests prove the whole shard meets the same clean rule'
scenarios: Promoting gates.py/validate.py to strict blocks on hundreds of subprocess-covered no-tests mutants.
Adding a function whose only coverage is a subprocess CLI golden trips ratchet's added/edited kill-every-mutant rule as no-tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Score against MAPPED mutants (killed/(killed+survived+timeout)) as in docs/mutation-testing.md, and either exclude no-tests from the blocking set or require an explicit per-shard 'subprocess-covered' annotation in the manifest so a no-tests mutant is only blocking when the shard declares in-process coverage as its contract.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name a per-shard runtime feasibility path for large shards (e.g. a documented per-shard time budget, proven narrower function scope, or reduced-mutant sampling) so a full base+head archive at --max-children 1 credibly completes within the 30-minute job limit, given the probe's signing.py 814-mutant / 108-unchecked-after-10-minutes evidence.
evidence: Plan: 'each with Python 3.12, mutmut==3.7.0, --max-children 1, the configured mutmut timeout, and a 30-minute job limit'

Ticket probe comment (2026-08-10): 'signing.py now generates 814 mutants ... After roughly ten minutes at --max-children 1, 108 were still unchecked' and 'A single 30-minute base+head all-shard job is also not credibly bounded.'
The advisory mode still requires a head archive; ratchet/strict require both base and head archives within the same bounded job.
findings.finding: The plan pins a 30-minute per-job limit for a matrix job that runs BOTH a fresh base and a fresh head mutation archive at `--max-children 1`, but the plan's own recorded probe shows this may be technically infeasible for the largest shards: signing.py generated 814 mutants and left 108 unchecked after roughly ten minutes of a single-sided run at `--max-children 1`, and the probe explicitly recorded that a base+head run is 'not credibly bounded'. The plan does not name how a large shard completes two full archives within one 30-minute job, nor a per-shard runtime budget or a smaller proven function-scope for such shards.
findings.location: Plan section 'The reusable workflow creates one matrix job per selected shard ... a 30-minute job limit' and 'compare fresh base/head archives'
scenarios: A change touches signing.py support/source, selecting the signing shard in ratchet mode; the 30-minute job cannot finish base+head archives and the job is killed, producing a spurious incomplete/blocking outcome or timing out with no evidence.
The weekly all-shard sweep runs the largest shards and repeatedly hits the wall-clock limit.
